newsitem.title: USA: Gillette's Buffett abstained on Duracell vote.
newsitem.headline: Gillette's Buffett abstained on Duracell vote.

text.p: Gillette Co director Warren Buffett abstained on the board's vote to approve a takeover of Duracell International Inc because he objected to the size of the fees involved, the companies said on Monday.

However, the Omaha, Neb., billionaire and his affiliates intend to vote their 10.8 percent of Gillette common stock in favor of the Gillette plan to issue some 109 million common shares as part of the Duracell deal, the companies said in a joint filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Shareholders of both companies will vote on the $7 billion transaction at meetings set for December 30.

Buffett was the only one of 12 Gillette directors who did not vote to approve the Duracell merger at the board's September 12 meeting, the filing said. The vote came shortly after Duracell directors approved the merger, it said.
While Buffett told the board he favored the merger, he objected to the $30 million investment banking and advisory fees payable by Duracell, the filing said.
Buffett believed the fee was excessive and noted that about 80 percent of Duracell fees effectively would be picked up by Gillette's pre-merger stockholders, it said.

In an earlier vote by the Gillette board, taken before Duracell directors voted, Buffett joined his fellow directors in unanimously approving the deal, provided that the fees were reduced to $18 million, according to the filing.

The Duracell board, which approved the deal unanimously, was told by special independent counsel that on a percentage basis the fees were about 0.39 percent of the value of the merger, which was within the range of 0.15 to 0.80 percent in recent large transactions, the filing said.
